TWENTY-FOURTH REPORT OF CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. 117 The duties to be performed by Mr. Pitts in the immediate office of the Sec- retary of the Treasury are of a confidential nature, and require a man having good judgment, tact, and a wide knowledge of public men. For these reasons the President issued the order. March 5, 1907. James G. Massey, of Maryland, may be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of the Interior without refereuce to civil-service rules. Mr. Massey was appointed to a clerkship in the Department of Commerce and I>abor in October, 1905, and in that Department was employed on work under the immediate direction of Commissioner James R. Garfield, at that time Com- missioner of Corporations. This work was of a more or less confidential nature. Mr. Garfield, as Secretary of the Interior, desired Mr. Massey's services in the Interior Department, but he was not eligible for transfer by reason of the three-year limitation imposed by statute. He therefore resigned his position in the Department of Commerce and Labor and was appointed in the Interior Department upon the order of the President. March 7, 1907. Mr. John C. Eversman, sr., a special examiner in the Peusion Office, may be appointed or transferred to a competitive position in that office. Mr. Eversman was appointed as a special examiner in the Pension Office under Schedule A of the civil-service rules, which excepts from the require- ment of examination five pension examiners to investigate fraudulent and other pension claims of a criminal nature. The Commissioner of Pensions desired to have Mr. Eversman covered into the classified service, and the Executive order allowing this was signed by the President. March 8, 1907. Mr. P. J. Hughes, who was separated from the Isthmian Canal Service on account of ill health and whose case is regarded by the Isthmian Canal Com- mission as particularly meritorious and deserving, may be reinstated and trans- ferred as a clerk to the War Department or one of its field branches. Mr. Hughes was selected on March 16, 1905, for api>ointment as clerk at $75 I>er month on the Isthmus of Panama through the clerk examination, and was discharged on April 27, 1900, from the position of clerk at $100 per month, the condition qf his health making such action necessary. His accumulated leave of absence was granted him and arrangements made for the payment of his sal- ary in the United States while on leave, such adjustment at that time being only authorized in exceptional and meritorious cases. The chief, office of administration, stated that he thought Mr. Hughes's case was deserving of special consideration. March 8, 1907. Mr. C. F. House may be appointed as clerk at $1,000 per annum, Naval Trnin lug Station, Great Lakes, North Chicago, 111., without compliance with the civil-service rules. The Navy Department had eudeavored to fill this vacancy through certiflcar tion for a period extending over five months, but had been unable to do so owing to the repeated declinations of the eligibles certified. The situation is isolated and the cost of living in the immediate vicinity is high, and it therefore seemed Impracticable to make an appointment through certification. Mr. House was formerly an enlisted man and a competent employee and was willing to accept the position.
